answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. A registry accepts one active identity per bond, and counterparties can challenge duplicate control with signed evidence; proven duplicates lose their bonds, while honest identities recover theirs after a delay. The inlet for participation stays open, but a cedar-like stake ties each account to real capital, so an attacker must immobilize funds for every Sybil and risks losing them. Cheap names alone cannot buy an oasis of influence.
